propositions: A store write that cannot acquire the write lock within its timeout budget is permanently discarded with no retry mechanism, resulting in data loss.

The lock acquisition deadline is computed as a single total_wait shared by both fcntl and mkdir legs, and attempts is a multiplier not a retry loop, so a timed-out acquire raises LockTimeout immediately.
Holder duration (60s-163s observed) now drives write loss more than writer count; when one holder exceeds the entire budget every waiter fails regardless of service order.

Bounded retry-with-backoff inside acquire() converts terminal loss into latency by re-attempting acquisition across multiple passes with jittered exponential backoff (0.5s, 1.0s, capped 2.0s) up to ~181.5s ceiling.
The retry is safe without double-write risk because LockTimeout is raised before the caller's write body executes; once acquire() returns the loop is finished and cannot re-enter.
Five call sites opt into retries via retries=_write_path_retries() reading REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES env (default 2, clamped [0,10]); all other callers keep fail-fast via retries=0 default unchanged.
